situation: Going to a fintech conference alone next week and I freeze up at the coffee breaks. Give me something to say to someone standing by the coffee.
reply: Hi, I'm Sam. Which session brought you here? I came for the fraud panel and half of it went over my head.
note: One question plus one line about you. The next question comes from their answer: 'What's the part people don't get about that?'

situation: 每周一在电梯里都会碰到隔壁部门的李姐，我只知道她上个月去新疆玩了。每次都尴尬地各自看手机。
reply: 李姐早！上个月去新疆，哪一站最值得去？
note: 记得对方说过的事最管用；接下来的问题从她的回答里找，别换话题。

situation: At my girlfriend's work party, chatting with a guy named Chris who's given me one-word answers twice now. How do I get out without it being awkward?
reply: I'm going to grab another drink. Good to meet you, Chris, enjoy the rest of the night.
note: Two flat answers is the cue. Exit warmly and don't make it a verdict on either of you.

situation: Meeting my boyfriend Arjun's dad for the first time at dinner on Saturday. Arjun says he's quiet and spends weekends restoring old Royal Enfield motorbikes in the garage. I want something to say that isn't about work.
reply: Arjun tells me you restore old Royal Enfields. Which one's in the garage at the moment?
note: Open on the thing he cares about, then let the next question come from his answer ("How long does one take, start to finish?") and share one small thing back before returning to him.

situation: First video call with my new team and I'm always early. It'll probably be just me and Inês, who's based in Lisbon, waiting for a few minutes. All I know is she's the data analyst.
reply: Hi Inês, looks like we're the early ones. I'm new this week, so I'll just ask: what's one thing about this team you wish someone had told you in your first month?
note: Asks for a view she actually has, which gives a thread to follow; the next question should come from her answer.

situation: 国庆回老家吃团圆饭，我旁边坐的是表姐的新老公，第一次见，只知道他在深圳做无人机。我怕冷场。
reply: 姐夫，听我姐说你在深圳做无人机？我一直挺好奇的，你们做的是航拍那种，还是送快递、给庄稼打药那种？
note: 问他有自己看法的事，然后顺着他的回答追问“当初怎么入的这行”；分享一句自己的，再把话头还给他。

situation: At my neighbour's barbecue I just asked a woman I met ten minutes ago, Grace, when her baby is due. She said 'I'm not pregnant' with a tight smile and now we're both standing by the grill in silence. What do I say right now?
reply: That came out wrong, and I'm sorry, I shouldn't have assumed. So how do you know Mark and Deb?
note: Fix it in one line and hand her a new thread straight away. A second apology makes the moment bigger than it was.

situation: Tomorrow I'm driving two hours with my new boss, Graham, to a client site in Leeds. I've been here three weeks and barely know him, except that he mentioned in my first week he's training for the York marathon. How do I start?
reply: So how's the training for York going? You mentioned it in my first week and I've been wondering how far the long runs are up to now.
note: Open with the one thing you remember, follow his answer ('What got you into running?'), share one small thing back, and on a long drive let a quiet stretch be quiet.

situation: On vient d'emménager à Lyon et je récupère ma fille à l'école tous les jours. Les autres parents se connaissent tous. Il y a un papa qui attend toujours au portail avec un grand chien roux, et ma fille ne parle que de ce chien.
reply: Bonjour ! Ma fille ne parle que de votre chien depuis la rentrée. Il s'appelle comment ?
note: Partir de ce qu'il y a sous les yeux, puis rebondir sur sa réponse et glisser une phrase sur vous (« On vient d'arriver de Nantes ») avant de lui rendre la parole.

situation: En la boda de mi prima en Sevilla me han sentado al lado del abuelo del novio, don Manuel, de 85 años. Solo sé que fue pescador en Cádiz toda la vida. No quiero pasar la cena en silencio.
reply: Don Manuel, me han contado que fue usted pescador en Cádiz toda la vida. ¿Qué es lo que más echa de menos del mar?
note: Pregunta por algo sobre lo que él tiene opinión, y saca la siguiente pregunta de su respuesta, no de una lista.

situation: Matched with Sam on Hinge. We've done 'how was your weekend' / 'good, you?' twice and it's dying. Their profile says they just got back from climbing in Kalymnos and are learning Greek 'badly'.
reply: Okay, I have to ask about Kalymnos. Was it the climbing that got you there, or did the Greek come first? I did a month of Duolingo Greek once and can mostly say 'the cat drinks milk'.
note: Swap generic questions for something they chose to show you, share one small thing back, and end on a question they'll enjoy answering.

situation: At a friend's housewarming on Saturday, someone will definitely ask 'so what do you do?' I was laid off from my bank job in August and haven't found anything yet. I don't want to lie or kill the conversation.
reply: Right now I'm between jobs. I was at Halden Bank for six years until August, and the upside is I've finally had time to learn to bake bread. How do you know Nadia?
note: One honest sentence, one small thing you'd happily talk about, then hand the thread back to them.

situation: 大学毕业十年的同学聚会上，一个男生特别热情地走过来叫出我的名字，还说记得我当年在辩论队。我完全想不起他叫什么，也不记得当年熟不熟。
reply: 你记性也太好了，连辩论队都记得！我得先坦白，十年没见，你的名字我一下卡住了，真不好意思，提醒我一下？你当年也常来看我们比赛吗？
note: 忘了名字就一句话坦白，别硬撑着聊；马上接住他给的话头，尴尬几秒就过去了。

situation: I'm picking up a client, Ji-woo Park, from her hotel tomorrow morning for the 20-minute drive to our Chicago office. She flew in from Seoul last night and it's her first time in the US. I don't want to talk shop the whole way or sit in silence.
reply: Welcome to Chicago, Ji-woo. How are you holding up after the flight? If you get a free evening while you're here, is there anything you're hoping to see or eat?
note: A visitor has a view on her own trip: follow her answer, offer one local tip of your own, then hand it back.

situation: I'm at the reception after my coworker Dana's dad's funeral. I never met him. I'm standing by the tea urn next to an older man I don't know and the silence is getting awkward.
reply: Hi, I'm Rob, I work with Dana. I never got to meet her dad. How did you know him?
note: At a funeral, invite a story rather than an opinion. If he shares one, 'What was he like?' keeps it going, and quiet moments can stay quiet.

situation: My sister's 15-year-old son Kai is staying with us this weekend and answers everything with 'fine' or a shrug. My sister told me he just started playing bass in a band with friends from school.
reply: Your mum says you've started playing bass in a band. What are you lot playing at the moment, covers or your own stuff?
note: Teenagers shut down at questions about school; ask about the thing they chose.
